claim: USCD's uncertainty-aware selective contrastive decoding improves average pass@1 code generation accuracy by 16.59% across HumanEval, MBPP, and MultiPL-E on five open-source code LLMs, using token-level uncertainty purely as an internal decoding-time gate.
stance_target: uncertainty signals can drive a downstream decoding ACTION with a measured accuracy payoff, even without being validated as a calibrated/communicable confidence score
scope_conditions: HumanEval, MBPP, MultiPL-E benchmarks; InCoder-6B, CodeLlama-7B, WizardCoder-15B, StarCoder, Llama2-7B
quoted_support: demonstrate that our proposed USCD significantly improves one-pass code generation, with an average pass@1 scores increase of 16.59%.

claim: The Jensen-Shannon divergence between token-distribution uncertainty (under a standard prompt) and output noise (elicited by a stripped-down 'lame prompt') is relatively low (~0.25), indicating the two are meaningfully correlated and justifying uncertainty as a gating signal for noise removal.
stance_target: token-level uncertainty correlates with hallucination/noise even if not a perfectly calibrated correctness probability
scope_conditions: preliminary study preceding the main USCD method
quoted_support: Our preliminary study shows that the Jensen-Shannon divergence (JS divergence) between token distribution uncertainty and the output noise is relatively low (approximately 0.25), indicating their high relevance.

claim: USCD is an inference-only, plug-and-play mechanism requiring no retraining or oracle test cases, only a modified negative prompt and standard token-level uncertainty at each decoding step.
stance_target: feasibility of single-GPU, inference-only uncertainty-driven interventions for code generation
scope_conditions: applies to any autoregressive code LLM at inference time
quoted_support: Notably, our proposed plug-and-play mechanism is an inference-only method, enjoying appealing flexibility.

claim: USCD never reports the calibration quality (AUROC, ECE) of the token-level uncertainty signal it exploits, and never exposes that uncertainty to a human end-user; it is used solely as an internal correction-strength gate.
stance_target: gap: internal utility of an uncertainty signal does not establish that the same signal would be trustworthy if communicated to a human
scope_conditions: inferred from abstract framing; full paper not accessed
quoted_support: we selectively eliminate output noise induced by lame prompts based on the uncertainty of the prediction distribution from the standard prompt.
